title: optimize-nccl-collectives-kvcache-overlap-tensor-parallel
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and tail latency by tuning NCCL collectives, stream priorities, and overlap between communication and KV-cache/kernel execution. Configurable rollout flag and fallback to previous scheduler.
description:
Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were seeing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and compute/kv-cache kernels on common generation workloads. This PR introduces a set of coordinated runtime changes to improve overlap, reduce stall time, and avoid sync points that block progress across ranks.

Summary: 1) Introduce a lightweight NCCL collective scheduling layer that assigns priorities to comm streams and enforces async collectives for all-reduce/all-gather patterns used in TP. 2) Adjust CUDA stream priorities and kernel launch ordering to prefer kv-cache writes/reads to stream 0 while issuing comms on a dedicated comm stream to increase concurrency. 3) Add a per-workload heuristic that delays non-critical kernel syncs when a pending collective is expected, avoiding unnecessary kernel/device syncs. 4) Add a continuous-batching-aware path: when continuous batching is enabled, the runtime aggregates small token batches across ranks and issues larger collectives to reduce per-token comm overhead. 5) Provide runtime flags and an opt-out environment variable to revert to previous behavior for canary rollout.

Changeset details: see commits and files changed below for granular diffs. Key behavior changes are gated behind runtime flags: TP_ASYNC_COLLECTIVES=true, TP_STREAM_PRIORITY_TUNE=auto, TP_CONT_BATCH_AGGREGATION=enabled. Default for hosted is enabled behind a canary percentage rollout in the control plane; Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in via config.

Benchmarks: end-to-end throughput improvements of 12-28% on 8xA100 40GB TP setups across GPT-like 2B-30B models with typical sequence lengths (512-1024) and continuous batching enabled. Median tail latency (p95) improved by 10-18% in our microbenchmark harness. We observed a ~6% regression in a degenerate allreduce-heavy synthetic pattern which is covered by the opt-out.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the scheduling logic, integration tests simulating TP rank startups, and multi-node perf test runs in perf-canary. Added regression tests to the eval-harness for token-level correctness. CI includes a multi-node NCCL smoke job (flaky tolerance added for transient infra flakes).

Rollout plan: 1) Canary on 5% of hosted TP clusters for 48 hours, monitor throughput, p95, NCCL error counters, and KV cache hit rates. 2) Expand to 25% if stable, then to 100% after 7 days. 3) For Dedicated, communicate change and offer opt-in. 4) Add automatic rollback to prior scheduler if NCCL error rate or p95 increases beyond thresholds.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps changes small in the hot path: scheduling decisions are O(1) and cached per model config. We also added telemetry hooks to trace overlap time and kernel wait time for future tuning.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Overall looks good. Can you add a fallback for drivers without stream priority support?
Ava Martinez (author): Good call - added a runtime check and fallback to round-robin comm streams when priorities unsupported (see nccl_scheduler.cpp:check_stream_priority()).
Riley Patel: The continuous batching aggregation could increase memory pressure. Did you measure peak memory?

Ava Martinez: Measured peak memory on 8xA100 runs; worst-case increase was ~3% at high batch aggregation thresholds. Added a soft cap and dynamic throttle to limit aggregation if device free memory < 8GB.
Sophia Nguyen: CI flaky on nccl smoke job - saw one transient failure on launch. Can we add retry/backoff?
Ava Martinez: Added a single retry with exponential backoff and increased wait for NCCL unique ID propagation. Also flagged the CI job as flaky-tolerant in the short term.
Riley Patel (approval): Approved after memory throttle and driver fallback additions.
Liam Chen (approval): Approved. Recommend post-merge telemetry dashboards.
Ops Bot: Canary rollout scheduled via control plane (5% -> 25% -> 100%), rollback threshold set to p95 +20% or NCCL_ERR_RATE > 0.5%
merge_details: post_merge_actions: deployed canary to 5% hosted TP clusters, created telemetry dashboards for tp_nccl_overlap and kv_cache_overlap_time
